doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Staying busy by playing every style, Jimmy Sturr
summary: Pallo says versatility keeps him working, from rock bands to Irish bands and Jimmy Sturr's polka band.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: What do you think of — here’s a big question — but what do you think of the music scene today? You don’t seem to have a lack of work. Right? You said before that work for you is not a problem.

No problem at all. I have no problem. And like January is supposed to be the slowest month for musicians. And I’ve been turning jobs down. And I presume Bucky is too and other musicians. And there are some that say, “Gee I only have two gigs this month” or three or four or whatever. I have too many. I’ve been turning some down. Because I guess a lot of it has to do with what you were asking me, how do I go from one venue to another, like if I have to go with a rock band, I’ll play with a rock band one night. The next night I may play with a trio that does Italian music let’s say. Then the next night I might play with an Irish band. Oh and then I also work with Jimmy Sturr who has a big band, he has 14, or I think he has 15 Grammys now.

The polka guy. But I don’t play polkas with him. When I’m with him he features me on whatever I would like to do. He calls me out and I come out and do 15, 20 minutes, and I’ll do songs like “Blue Skies,” “Twilight Time” I’ll play on the guitar, and I’ll do “How High the Moon,” Les Paul style. You know people love that. So that’s I think the difference, because if you’re just going to stay on one path and you’re just going to play jazz let’s say, you’re limited then.

You have to wait for someone to call you for that gig. So that’s why I keep changing every — and then I use the different guitars. That’s how, if you’re going to play with Jimmy I’ll bring my 335 or I might bring an acoustic with electric of course on it. And with Keith I bring a Les Paul, and so forth. Oh the Squirrel Nut Zippers, have you ever heard of them?
